Team / Alex,

As I pulled together the QBR narrative this morning I hit a coverage gap on our Hosted SLA expansion ask. The ask the field is expecting for the QBR slide is: a clear executive rationale + committed resourcing cadence (Q3 ramp) + an ask for a formal pilot with Acme. Right now our internal roadmap bullets don't align to that level of clarity.

Quick asks so we can lock the slide by EOD Tuesday:
- Aditya: note the executive rationale (one-paragraph) we want on the slide and the pricing tradeoffs for a pilot.
- Marissa: confirm what infra/headcount we can commit to Q3 ramp (rough FTE + infra ops) and any redlines.
- Grace: any known compliance/questions from Acme (or PartnerCloud) that would block pilot sign-off?
- Jonas: messaging/order of priorities for execs + a 1-line ask for the CEO slide.

Alex / Sara (PartnerCloud) — if you have a one-liner we should include on the ask side (e.g., pilot objectives), please send it back to this thread.

Attachment: QBR-roadmap-highlights.pdf (slide stub)

Thanks — I want this to read tight and not handwave on commitments.

--

Lauren — thanks for flagging. Quick draft of the exec rationale and pricing notes below (can be condensed to one line for the slide):

Executive rationale (draft): Redwood's dedicated-hosted SLA expands enterprise adoption by guaranteeing predictable latency and capacity for latency-sensitive workflows — reducing customer TCO through caching/batching optimizations while providing a clear upgrade path from shared-hosted plans.

Pricing tradeoffs / pilot framing: we recommend a 3-month pilot at a discounted committed rate (20% off list) with a clear evaluation metric: 99th percentile latency target and cost-per-infer token threshold. If pilot metrics meet targets, move to a 12-month reserved commit. (Deal ID: RED-8421)

Questions that affect the slide:
- Is the 20% pilot discount something leadership is comfortable pre-approving?
- Will we offer a credit for migration engineering time?

Alex: happy to include a single line to signal Acme's commitment if you confirm.

On the operational side: the cost model assumes current quantization benefits and autoscaling. If Marissa can't commit to the Q3 capacity, I'll flag the pricing/commit ask as contingent.

--
Aditya Rao
Head of Revenue Operations
